newsitem.title: USA: U.S. industry keeps growing steadily in June.
newsitem.headline: U.S. industry keeps growing steadily in June.

text.p: Production by U.S. mines, factories and utilities kept growing steadily in June, the Federal Reserve said on Wednesday, boosted by stronger output of new cars, aircraft and computers.
Overall industrial production increased 0.3 percent last month after a 0.2 percent May gain as industries once again ran at 83.5 percent of their maximum operating capacity, the same as in May.

"Continued strength in commercial aircraft and the high-technology sector again contributed importantly to the growth of output," the Fed said, as did a rebound in motor vehicle production from strike-depressed levels in April and May.

Manufacturing industries increased their production in June by 0.3 percent, the same as in both April and May. The Fed said that much of the manufacturing vigour in recent months came from increased output of costly and long-lasting durable goods. It noted especially strong increases in July production of electrical machinery and transportation equipment.
Production by utility companies gained by 0.4 percent in June after a 2.7 percent May plunge as warmer weather pushed up demand for electricity for air conditioning.
At mining companies, production was flat in June, but that followed a 1.9 percent surge in May output
Previously, the Fed reported that May industrial production had climbed more strongly, by 0.4 percent, but it revised that downward.
Economist Charles Lieberman of Chase Securities Inc. in New York said the industrial output report again confirmed little or no threat to the steady economic expansion from inflation.
"It shows moderate growth," Lieberman said, "Respectable, moderate growth."

Similarly, economist Josh Feinman at Bankers Trust Co. in New York said it indicated the industrial sector was not facing sharp price rises that could put pressure on the Federal Reserve to boost interest rates.
"There is nothing in here to get in the way of the market feeling that the Federal Reserve is on hold and the good times can continue," Feinman said.
The Fed has held rates steady at its past two policy-setting sessions in May and July. Its Federal Open Market Committee is next scheduled to meet on Aug. 19.
